summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease status post kidney transplant, and severe peripheral vascular disease was admitted for severe left leg pain due to necrotic infection and gangrene. He underwent a two-stage left below-knee amputation: first a guillotine amputation followed by re-amputation with closure. He received blood transfusions preoperatively to support hemoglobin levels and was treated with intravenous vancomycin, ciprofloxacin, and metronidazole for infection, later transitioning to oral antibiotics. Pain was managed with a Dilaudid PCA initially, then oral hydromorphone, acetaminophen, and pregabalin. The nephrology team optimized tacrolimus and blood pressure medications to protect his transplant. The wound healed well, and he was discharged to extended care with plans for rehabilitation and outpatient follow-up. His right hand showed dry gangrene of multiple digits, but no acute intervention was needed.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities with gangrene, left leg
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
